metric.definition: The share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak.

reading.body:
Server utilization rate measures the share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at a single peak moment.

Idle servers are described as burning power, licenses, and depreciation while producing nothing, and fleet utilization is named as where the money hides in most enterprise estates, functioning as the denominator that makes every other efficiency metric honest, a facility can report an excellent PUE while running servers that spend most of their time idle, a form of waste that power-overhead metrics alone would never surface.

Its siblings, stranded power and space per cabinet and floor loading limits, are grouped under Capacity and server use, together measuring how much of a facility's provisioned resources, power, space, and compute itself, actually translate into productive work.

siblings.label: Stranded power and space per cabinet
